svg.text: Aegis governed-agent architecture — what is actually verified
Benefits eligibility pack · from-zero gate run ben-fpg (2026-09-10), us-east-1, single account · AWS account id redacted to 111122223333 throughout

How to read this. Green = demonstrated on a from-zero live run and named by the gate check that proves it. Amber = the code exists and is unit-tested, but no live run has demonstrated it. Grey = deliberately not ours: stubbed in the manifest, or the adopter's to own. A picture that showed
only the green boxes would be a sales diagram, not an architecture.
Two proof users per run, removed at teardown.
CONN-1 — governed outbound to a system of record
Measure the artifact, not the source.
Every green box was read back from AWS after the
run, or from the synthesized template - never from
the code that was supposed to produce it. Three
separate defects in this build were invisible in
the source and obvious in the artifact: users the
IaC path never creates, an authorizer that trusts
exactly one client, and a Lambda environment left
empty because a label contained a comma.
CONN-1 took six from-zero live runs. Not one of
the six failures was where it appeared to be:
fpa authentication - proof users the CDK
fpb the gateway - the authorizer allow-lists
fpd no diagnosis at all - the error went
fpe the SoR trusted nothing - EXPECTED_ISS
was empty; six retries failed silently
Each was hidden behind a silenced error path. CI
now fails when a new one appears.
THE TWO SENTENCES THAT BELONG TOGETHER, AND SHOULD NEVER BE QUOTED APART
The system of record is a REAL OAuth2 API with RS256/JWKS signature verification. IT IS OURS.
Proving the governed path reaches it is not proving a customer's system of record has been governed.
connect_system_of_record stays stubbed in the manifest for exactly that reason. Standing this connector up
against our own mock took six live runs; a real integration adds the customer's IdP, network boundary, token
lifetimes and change control on top of that. The governance is reusable. The integration is engineering work.
Step 3 of the connector proof denies an outsider, and
the denial NAMES require_tenant - a specific policy.
An earlier run denied the outsider and the legitimate
reviewer with the same string. 'Outsider denied' proved
nothing then, because everything was denied.
A deny-by-default claim is only evidence when the
